key_insight: A basal magma ocean can turn lunar tides into resonant interfacial waves that drive much stronger core flow than standard tidal forcing models predict.
engineering_relevance: The theory links lunar evolution and core structure to geodynamo power, offering a mechanism that could help explain early magnetic field generation in differentiated planets.
method: Model the Earth's liquid-metal core overlain by a basal magma ocean as two immiscible layers separated by a density interface.
Derive the tidal response in the inviscid limit and identify a resonance when forcing frequency matches the interfacial-mode natural frequency.
Add finite viscosity and coupled lunar recession/BMO crystallization parameterizations to estimate flow speed, ellipticity, and instability metrics over time.
evidence_signal: The paper presents a theoretical analysis supported by parameterized evolutionary models, showing amplified tidal coupling and enhanced instability indicators near resonance rather than experimental or observational data.
watch_item: The predictions depend on uncertain early-Earth parameters such as BMO properties, viscosity, lunar recession history, and the timing of crystallization.
paper_title: Resonant lunar tides of Earth's core and basal magma ocean
